Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. 霧島神宮 | image = Kirishimashrine.jpg | caption = The ''[[honden]]'' | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|31|51|32.2|N|130|52|18.7|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Konohanasakuya-hime]]

[[Toyotama-hime]]
[[Ugayafukiaezu]]

Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden |location = 2608-5 Kirishima Taguchi, Kirishima City, Kagoshima Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|31|51|32.2|N|130|52|18.7|E|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] |rank = Shikinaisha (minor), former Kanpei-taisha, Beppyo Shrine |established = Traditionally during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century)
Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. National Treasure]] "Kirishima Jingu" (September 25, 2022, [[NHK-BS Premium|NHK-BSP]]){{Cite web|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Jingu Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden |location = 2608-5 Kirishima Taguchi, Kirishima City, Kagoshima Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|31|51|32.2|N|130|52|18.7|E|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] |rank = Shikinaisha (minor), former Kanpei-taisha, Beppyo Shrine |established = Traditionally during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century)
Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Third Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kagura Hall == Access == {{section-stub}} == Documentary == * [[Welcome to the National Treasure]] "Kirishima Jingu" (September 25, 2022, [[NHK-BS Premium|NHK-BSP]]){{Cite web|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Jingu |date=September 25, 2022 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=September 25, 2022 |accessdate=September 25, 2022}} == References == === Sources === {{Reflist|30em}} == {{神社 |名称 = 霧島神宮 |画像 = [[ファイル:Kirishima-Jingu Front.jpg|270px]]
勅使殿・拝殿・本殿 |所在地 = [[鹿児島県]][[霧島市]]霧島田口2608番地5号 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|31|51|32.2|N|130|52|18.7|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ニニギ|天饒石国饒石天津日高彦火瓊瓊杵尊]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）[[論社]]
旧[[官幣大社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建 = 伝[[欽明天皇]]朝（[[6世紀]]）
伝[[欽明天皇]]元年（[[540年]]） |本殿 = [[入母屋造]] |別名 = |札所等 = 霧島六社権現 |例祭 = [[9月19日]] |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=霧島神宮|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''霧島神宮'''（きりしまじんぐう）は[[鹿児島県]][[霧島市]]霧島田口にある[[神社]]。[[延喜式内社]]の[[論社]]であり、[[旧社格]]は[[官幣大社]][http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html 霧島神宮] - 鹿児島県神社庁 2012年2月27日。本殿、幣殿、拝殿は[[国宝]]に指定されている令和4年2月9日文部科学省告示第9号。。 == 祭神 == 現在の祭神は次の7柱[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html ご由緒]（公式サイト）。。 ; 主祭神 :* [[ニニギ|天饒石国饒石天津日高彦火瓊瓊杵尊]] ; 相殿神 :* [[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花開姫尊]] :* [[ホオリ|彦火火出見尊]] :* [[トヨタマヒメ|豊玉姫尊]] :* [[ウガヤフキアエズ|鵜鶿草葺不合尊]] :* [[タマヨリビメ (日向神話)|玉依姫尊]] :* [[神武天皇|神倭磐余彦尊]] == 歴史 == [[ファイル:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|古宮址]] [[ファイル:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|神木の杉]] [[欽明天皇]]の御代（6世紀）、慶胤（けいいん）上人という僧侶が[[高千穂峰]]と[[御鉢|火常峰（御鉢）]]の間の「瀬多尾（せたお）（背門丘・瀬戸尾）」に社殿を造られたのが始まりとされる{{Cite book|和書 |title=角川日本地名大辞典46鹿児島県 |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=角川書店}}。一説に[[欽明天皇]]元年（[[540年]]）の創建ともいわれている{{Cite book|和書 |title=ふるさとのお社 鹿児島県神社誌 |date=1995-04-30 |year=1995 |publisher=鹿児島県神道青年会}}。 [[高千穂峰]]が日本神話の[[天孫降臨]]の伝承地とされる事から、現在は[[日向三代]]にまつわる神々が祀られているが、元々は[[高千穂峰]]そのものを信仰の対象とする[[山岳信仰]]から始まった神社であると考えられる{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}。 元の社地の瀬多尾は、火口に近い場所であったため社殿は噴火でたびたび炎上し、[[延暦]]7年（[[788年]]）7月の[[御鉢|火常峰（御鉢）]]の噴火で焼失した。 その後[[天慶]]3年（[[940年]]）、あるいは[[村上天皇]]の御代の[[天暦]]4年（[[950年]]）に[[性空]]上人により瀬多尾越（現在の[[高千穂河原]]・古宮址）に再興されるが、ここもたびたび噴火の巻き添えで炎上し、[[文暦]]元年（[[1234年]]）の[[御鉢|火常峰（御鉢）]]の大噴火により社殿、僧坊等がことごとく焼失したため、[[霧島市]]霧島田口の待世（霧島中学校の隣、[[霧島町]]グランドとの境）に「仮宮」を建てて、約250年間祭っていた。 [[文明_(日本)|文明]]16年（[[1484年]]）、[[島津忠昌]]の命により兼慶（けんけい）上人が再興したのが、現在の霧島神宮である。ただし、社殿はその後も幾度も炎上し、現在の社殿は[[正徳 (日本)|正徳]]５年（[[1715年]]）、[[島津吉貴]]の奉納により再建した物である。 また一説には、[[文暦]]元年（[[1234年]]）の噴火で社殿を焼失した後、社殿を[[霧島山]]の東の長尾山（現在の'''東霧島神社'''の地）に移しその後、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]16年（[[1484年]]）、[[島津忠昌]]がこれを「東社」（'''霧島東御在所権現'''、現在の'''霧島東神社'''）と「西社」（'''西御在所霧島権現'''、現在の'''霧島神宮'''）の2社に分けたともいわれている{{Cite book|和書 |title=新装普及版 神社辞典 |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=東京堂出版}}。 またこれ以外にも、社殿を[[霧島山]]の東の長尾山に移した後、現在の'''[[霧島岑神社]]'''と'''霧島東神社'''の2社に分け、更に'''霧島東神社'''から'''霧島西神社'''（現在の'''霧島神宮'''）を分けたという説もある{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}。 歴代[[島津氏]]の尊崇篤く、[[島津義久]]は、[[天正]]6年（[[1578年]]）[[耳川の戦い]]に臨む途中に参拝して[[くじ|鬮]]を引き、また九州北上にあたっても天正14年（[[1585年]]）6月に[[日向国]]惣先達職の[[面高善哉坊]]と重臣[[山田有信]]を、再び9月に[[吉田清存]]を、それぞれ遣わして鬮を引き侵攻方面を決めるなど、重要事の決定に際したびたび神慮を仰いでいる{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}。 また、[[坂本龍馬]]が日本最初といわれる新婚旅行で[[霧島連峰]]を訪れたことが知られるが、その頃にはすでに山頂には天津日高彦火瓊瓊杵尊が突き刺したという[[天の逆鉾]]があった坂本龍馬{{青空文庫|000908|51734|新字旧仮名|手紙−慶応二年十二月四日　坂本乙女あて−}}。 明治期の[[神仏分離令]]が発令されるまでは'''西御在所霧島権現'''と称し、本地堂は十一面観音。別当寺に華林寺を有する。霧島山を中心とした修験僧による[[霧島六所権現]]信仰の中心的役割を果たしていた{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}。 [[近代社格制度]]のもと、[[1874年]]（[[明治]]7年）2月に[[官幣大社]]に列格された。 [[1935年]]（昭和10年）[[11月16日]]、[[陸軍特別大演習]]終了後、[[昭和天皇]]が[[行幸]]{{Cite book |和書 |author=原武史 |title=昭和天皇御召列車全記録 |publisher=新潮社 |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}。 また、[[神木]]の[[スギ|杉]]は樹齢約800年と推定され、南九州の杉の祖先ともいわれている{{要出典|date=2022年2月}}。 令和4年2月9日の官報告示により、「本殿、幣殿、拝殿」が国宝に指定された[https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shitebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html 霧島市公式ホームページ 指定文化財の概要【霧島】]。 == 祭祀 == 年間約100もの祭儀が行われている。 * 朔日祭（ついたちさい）　毎月1日 * 月次祭（つきなみさい）　毎月19日 * 歳旦祭　1月1日 * 初日供祭（はつにっくさい）　1月2日 * 元始祭　1月3日 * 散籾祭（うちまきさい）　2月18日（旧暦1月1日） * 御田植祭　3月3日（旧暦2月4日） * 狭名田の長田御田植祭（さなだのおさだおたうえさい）　6月第一日曜 * 大祓式　6月30日、12月31日 * 南九州御神楽　8月最終土曜 * 例祭　9月19日 * 除夜祭　12月31日 == 文化財 == === 国宝 === * 本殿・幣殿・拝殿 1棟（附 棟札2枚）（建造物） - 2022年（令和4年）2月9日指定。 === 重要文化財 === * 登廊下 * 勅使殿 （以下は「附」（つけたり）指定） * 門守神社　2棟 * 神饌所　1棟 ファイル:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|勅使殿（側面） ファイル:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|拝殿 ファイル:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|登廊下 以上の社殿は鹿児島藩主[[島津吉貴]]の寄進で、正徳5年（1715年）に建立された。社殿はいずれも朱塗りの華麗なものである。特に本殿は内部も豪華に装飾され、柱、梁、長押などはすべて朱漆塗りとした上に要所を彩色文様や鍍金の飾り金具で装飾し、壁には極彩色の浮き彫りを施した羽目板を配するなど、贅をこらしている。[[神社建築]]で、外部だけでなく内部までこのように装飾をこらしたものは珍しく、「'''西の日光'''」と言う別名を持つ。 == 境内 == もともと[[霧島山]]一帯が霧島神宮の境内であったが、明治4年（[[1871年]]）の[[廃藩置県]]の際に霧島山の頂上に沿って県境が引かれ、[[宮崎県]]側は神宮境内から外された。明治15年（[[1882年]]）にはさらに7810ヘクタールが削減され、[[昭和]]21年（[[1946年]]）の[[日本国憲法]]制定による宗教法人化で山林の大部分は国有地となった。その後、祭典行事に必要な789ヘクタールが神宮へ返還されている霧島町郷土誌編集委員会編　『霧島町郷土誌』　霧島町、1992年。。 Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Third Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kagura Hall == Access == {{section-stub}} == Documentary == * [[Welcome to the National Treasure]] "Kirishima Jingu" (September 25, 2022, [[NHK-BS Premium|NHK-BSP]]){{Cite web|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Jingu |date=September 25, 2022 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=September 25, 2022 |accessdate=September 25, 2022}} == References == === Sources === {{Reflist|30em}} == Related Literature == * Yasushi Anzu, Yoshihiko Umeda (Eds.), 'Shinto Dictionary', Jinja Shinpōsha, 1968, p.25 * Eiji Shirai, Masaaki Toki (Eds.), 'Shrine Dictionary', Tokyo-do Publishing, 1979, pp. 120-121 * Haruhira Ueyama et al., 'Japan Shrine General Encyclopedia', Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 1992, pp. 282-283 * 'The Book of Shinto', Gakken, 1992, p.227 * Taichi Tatsunomiya, Yoko Nakamura, Haruo Nakano, "Energizing Shrines - Sixth Episode: Kirishima Jingu", 'Psiko' June Issue, Poplar Publishing, 2006 * 'Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia', Kadokawa Shoten, 1983 * 'Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette', Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association, 1995 * Eiji Shirai, Masaaki Toki (Eds.), 'New Edition of Shrine Encyclopedia', Tokyo-do Publishing, 1997 == See also == Christians in the Satsuma Domain, and Ikko Sect followers pretended to be parishioners of Kirishima Jingu to avoid persecution. * [[Tanzan Shrine]]: A shrine known as "Nikko of the Kansai region" * The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[940]] or [[950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.
