Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. '''Kirishima Jingu''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]]. == Shikinaisha (式内社) == {| class="wikitable sortable" ! District !! Name !! Funding category !! Shrine DB |- | RONSHA || {{ill|Kirishima Jingu|lt=Kirishima Jingū|en|Kirishima Shrine|ja|霧島神宮|commons|Category:Kirishima-jingu|fr|Kirishima-jingū|zh|霧島神宮|WD=Q704622}} || {{ill|Kokuhei-sha (Engishiki Jinmyocho)|WD=Q135160342|lt=Kokuhei|comment=categorized}} || — || — || {{ill|Kirishimano Shrine|lt=Kirishimano Shrine|WD=Q135041487}}; {{ill|Kirishimano Shrine|lt=Kirishimano Shrine|WD=Q135041487}} || {{coord|31.858641|130.871321|display=inline}} || [https://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=183327 DB] |} {{wikidata link|Q704622}} == Accidentally Overwritten Content == {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kirishima-Jingū

Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden |location = 2608-5 Kirishima Taguchi, Kirishima City, Kagoshima Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|31|51|32.2|N|130|52|18.7|E|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] |Rank = Shikinaisha (minor), former Kanpei-taisha, Beppyo Shrine |established = Traditionally during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century)
Traditionally in the 1st year of Emperor Kinmei (540) |main_building_style = Irimoya-zukuri |other_names = |fudasho = Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine |annual_festival = September 19 |rituals = |map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Jingu|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|frame-width=200}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. [[Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}} Historically, the entire of [[Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[volcanic]] [[eruption]]s. ==Overview== '''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. It is a designated [[Shikinaisha]] (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012 == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website] ; Main deity :* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]] ; Deities enshrined together :* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]] :* [[Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]] :* [[Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]] :* [[Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]] == History == [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]] According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}} Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}} Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship. The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions. In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later. In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[Shimazu Tadamasa]]. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]]. Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}} Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine. The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns. [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}} Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners. In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system. On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}} The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees. == festivals == Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu. * Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month * Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month * Saitan-sai - January 1 * Hatsuniku-sai - January 2 * Genshi-sai - January 3 * Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year) * Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4) * Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June * Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31 * Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August * festival - September 19 * Joyasai - December 31 == Cultural Properties == === National Treasures === * Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.. === Important Cultural Properties === * Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor) * Chokushiden (In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties) * Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings) * Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building) File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West." == Precincts == The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992. {{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]].

[[:en:Takachiho-gawara|Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="env.go.jp">{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

Historically, the entire of [[:en:Mount Kirishima|Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds.

It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] [[:en:Eruption|Eruption]]s.

==Overview==

'''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012</ref>

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:<ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website]</ref>
; Main deity
:* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]]
; Deities enshrined together
:* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]]

== History ==
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]]
According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[:en:Otake|Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref> Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>

Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.<ref></ref>

The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[:en:Shimazu Tadamasa|Shimazu Tadamasa]].<ref name=":0" /> The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]].<ref name=":0" />

Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}}</ref> Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.<ref></ref>

The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.<ref></ref>

[[:en:Sakamoto Ryoma|Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.<ref>Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}}</ref>

Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.<ref></ref> In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system.

On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>

The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.<ref></ref>

== festivals ==
Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu.
* Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month
* Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month
* Saitan-sai - January 1
* Hatsuniku-sai - January 2
* Genshi-sai - January 3
* Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year)
* Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4)
* Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June
* Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31
* Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August
* festival - September 19
* Joyasai - December 31

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
* Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.</ref>.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor)
* Chokushiden
(In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties)
* Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings)
* Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building)
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor
</gallery>
These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West."

== Precincts ==
The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[:en:Constitution of Japan|Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.<ref>Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.</ref>

{{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]].

[[:en:Takachiho-gawara|Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="env.go.jp">{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

Historically, the entire of [[:en:Mount Kirishima|Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds.

It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] [[:en:Eruption|Eruption]]s.

==Overview==

'''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012</ref>

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:<ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website]</ref>
; Main deity
:* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]]
; Deities enshrined together
:* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]]

== History ==
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]]
According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[:en:Otake|Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref> Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>

Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.<ref></ref>

The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[:en:Shimazu Tadamasa|Shimazu Tadamasa]].<ref name=":0" /> The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]].<ref name=":0" />

Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}}</ref> Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.<ref></ref>

The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.<ref></ref>

[[:en:Sakamoto Ryoma|Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.<ref>Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}}</ref>

Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.<ref></ref> In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system.

On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>

The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.<ref></ref>

== festivals ==
Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu.
* Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month
* Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month
* Saitan-sai - January 1
* Hatsuniku-sai - January 2
* Genshi-sai - January 3
* Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year)
* Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4)
* Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June
* Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31
* Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August
* festival - September 19
* Joyasai - December 31

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
* Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.</ref>.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor)
* Chokushiden
(In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties)
* Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings)
* Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building)
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor
</gallery>
These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West."

== Precincts ==
The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[:en:Constitution of Japan|Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.<ref>Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.</ref>

{{Nihongo|'''Kirishima-Jingū'''|霧島神宮}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kirishima, Kagoshima|Kirishima]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]].

[[:en:Takachiho-gawara|Takachiho-gawara]] the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="env.go.jp">{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

Historically, the entire of [[:en:Mount Kirishima|Mount Kirishima]] is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds.

It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Properties]], such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] [[:en:Eruption|Eruption]]s.

==Overview==

'''Kirishima Jingu''' (霧島神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Kirishima Taguchi, [[Kirishima City]], [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is a designated {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor), and its former status was Kanpei-taisha (Imperial shrine of the first Rank).<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Jingu] - Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Agency, February 27, 2012</ref>

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:<ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website]</ref>
; Main deity
:* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]]
; Deities enshrined together
:* [[Kono-hana-sakuya-hime|Konohanasakuya-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Toyotama-hime|Toyotama-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[Ugaya|Ugaya no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Tamayori-hime|Tamayori-hime no mikoto]]
:* [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Jinmu-tenno]]

== History ==
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]]
According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater [[:en:Otake|Otake]], known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref> Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>

Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.<ref></ref>

The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in [[:en:940|940]] or [[:en:950|950]] by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1234|1234]], another major eruption destroyed the shrine, and it was moved to its current location in Kirishima Taguchi, about 250 years later.<ref name=":0" />

In [[:en:1484|1484]], the shrine was rebuilt by Kenkei, under the orders of [[:en:Shimazu Tadamasa|Shimazu Tadamasa]].<ref name=":0" /> The current shrine buildings were rebuilt in [[:en:1715|1715]] by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]].<ref name=":0" />

Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}}</ref> Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.<ref></ref>

The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the [[:en:Battle of Mimigawa|Battle of Mimigawa]] in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.<ref></ref>

[[:en:Sakamoto Ryoma|Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.<ref>Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}}</ref>

Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.<ref></ref> In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system.

On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>

The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.<ref></ref>

== festivals ==
Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu.
* Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month
* Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month
* Saitan-sai - January 1
* Hatsuniku-sai - January 2
* Genshi-sai - January 3
* Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year)
* Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4)
* Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June
* Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31
* Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August
* festival - September 19
* Joyasai - December 31

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
* Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.</ref>.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor)
* Chokushiden
(In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties)
* Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings)
* Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building)
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor
</gallery>
These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West."

== Precincts ==
The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the [[:en:Abolition of the han system|Abolition of the han system]] in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the [[:en:Constitution of Japan|Constitution of Japan]] in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.<ref>Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.</ref>
