Legendary {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} 1st year ({{jalink|540 years|Q30900}}) |Main shrine = {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = Kirishima Rokusha Gongen |Regular festival = {{jalink|September 19th|Q2896}} |Shinto ritual =|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}} of {{jalink|Engishikinaisha}}, and {{jalink|old company rank}} is {{jalink|Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}}Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. . === Enshrined God === The following seven deities are currently enshrined [http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* {{jalink|Ninigi|Q1056017|Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi}} ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Konohananosakuyabime|Q1781862|Konohana Kahimeson}} :* {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hikohihodemison}} :* {{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Himeson}} :* {{jalink|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|Uro Kusabuki Fugoson}} :* {{jalink|Tamayoribime (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayorihime no Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188|Kamiwa Iwayohiko}} === History === [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]] During the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}}. {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)}}{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} ({{jalink|540|Q30900}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}.{{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} is said to be the place where {{jalink|descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{jalink|three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{jalink|mountain cult|Q93697439}}, where {{jalink|mountain worship|Q93697439}} worshiped {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} itself. The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Hōjomine (Ohachi)}} in July of {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} ({{jalink|788|Q30721}}).After that, {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}}3 years ({{jalink|940|Q23830}}) or {{jalink|Tenryaku|Q1346281}}4 during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Murakami|Q374015}} In the year ({{jalink|950|Q23449}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{jalink|Takachiho River|Q10566710}}, old palace ruins) by {{jalink|Sekora|Q11491623}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the large eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Kajomine (Ohachi)}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{jalink|Kirishima Town|Q6415332}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years..{{jalink|Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|Civilization}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{jalink|Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537}} as a dedication. Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}, the current '''{{jalink|Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''. Respected by the successive {{jalink|Shimazu clan|Q1061406}}, {{jalink|Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727}} was born in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|15 In 1978|Q6707}}) {{jalink|Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{jalink|lottery|Q5433694|a wig}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{jalink|1585|Q6736}}) In June, {{jalink|Yontaka Zenyabo}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{jalink|Arinobu Yamada|Q80475 88}} and again in September, {{jalink|Kiyōyoshi Yoshida}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{jalink|Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450}} visited the {{jalink|Kirishima Mountain Range}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}. Until the {{jalink|Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{jalink|Kirishima Rokusho Gongen}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}. Under the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}), it was ranked as {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (1935) {{jalink|November 16|Q3029}}, after {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}} {{jalink|Yukiyuki|Q11626055}}{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.Also, the {{jalink|sacred tree|Q48743901}} {{jalink|cedar|Q147388|cedar}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}. According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]. === Rituals === Approximately 100 rituals are held annually. * Tsukutachisai (first day of every month) * Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month * Saitan Festival January 1st * Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd) * Genshi Festival January 3rd * Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar) * Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June * Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st * Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August * Regular festival September 19th * New Year's Eve Festival December 31st === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4). === Important cultural property === * Climbing corridor * Imperial Envoy Hall (The following is designated as “attached”) * Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings * 1 sacred food hall File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{jalink|Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{jalink|Shinto architecture|Q3080012}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''. === Precincts === Originally, the {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{jalink|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{jalink|1882|Q7812}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}21 ({{jalink|1946|Q18610}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{jalink|Constitution of Japan|Q237082}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. . File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Ninotorii File:Kirishima Shrine (Torii).jpg|Three Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kaguraden === Access === ; bus *{{jalink|Kyushu Railway|Q498366|JR}}{{jalink|Nippo Main Line|Q1052288}} Get off at {{jalink|Kirishima Jingu Station|Q6415333}} and take the {{jalink|Kagoshima Kotsu|Q11676491}} bus bound for Kirishima Iwasaki Hotel, then take the bus for about 15 minutes. *About 1 hour after taking the Kagoshima Kotsu Kirishima Shrine Access Bus from {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}}. ; car *{{jalink|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803}} Get off at {{jalink|Yokogawa Interchange|Q1655302}}, {{jalink| About 40 minutes via Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50 Makizono Satsuma Line |Q11676950|Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50}} and {{jalink|National Route 223|Q6156973}}. === Documentary === * {{jalink|Welcome to the National Treasure}} "Kirishima Shrine" (September 25, 2022, {{jalink|NHK-BS Premium||NHK-BSP}}) {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Shrine |date=2022-09-25 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=2022-09-25 |accessdate=2022-09-25}} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 25 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{jalink|Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645}}, 1979, pp. 120-121 *Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{jalink|Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 282-283 * "Book of Shinto" {{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|Gakken}}, 1992, p. 227 * Taichi Tatsumiya, Yoko Nakamura, and Haruo Nakano, “Shrines that give you energy - Vol. 6 Kirishima Shrine,” “Psiko” June issue, {{jalink|Poplar Publishing|Q3908386}}, 2006 * "Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture" {{jalink|Kadokawa Shoten|Q1054765}}, 1983 * “Furusato no Osha Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Journal” Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association, 1995 * Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki (eds.), New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary, Tokyodo Publishing, 1997 === Related items === {{WikiCommons|Category:Kirishima-jingu}} {{Osm box|n|2483574061}} * {{jalink|Takachiho Kawara|Q10566710}} * {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}} * {{jalink|Ikko sect|Q5366010}}: {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, {{jalink|Satsuma domain|Q676187}} cracked down on Ikko sect more strictly than {{jalink|Christian|Q718714}}, and the Ikko sect pretended to be parishioners of Kirishima Shrine. * {{jalink|Tanzan Shrine|Q488618}}: A shrine called the “Nikko of Kansai” * {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu Shrine|Q696641}} === External link === * [https://kirishimajingu.or.jp/ Kirishima Jingu] (Jingu official) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirishima Shinkuu}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:鹿児島県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:官幣大社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:鹿児島県の国宝]] [[Category:鹿児島県の重要文化財]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (建造物)]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:霧島市の建築物]] [[Category:霧島市の歴史]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:Need translation]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqq]]

Legendary {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} 1st year ({{jalink|540 years|Q30900}}) |Main shrine = {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = Kirishima Rokusha Gongen |Regular festival = {{jalink|September 19th|Q2896}} |Shinto ritual =|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}} of {{jalink|Engishikinaisha}}, and {{jalink|old company rank}} is {{jalink|Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}}Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. . === Enshrined God === The following seven deities are currently enshrined [http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* {{jalink|Ninigi|Q1056017|Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi}} ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Konohananosakuyabime|Q1781862|Konohana Kahimeson}} :* {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hikohihodemison}} :* {{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Himeson}} :* {{jalink|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|Uro Kusabuki Fugoson}} :* {{jalink|Tamayoribime (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayorihime no Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188|Kamiwa Iwayohiko}} === History === [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]] During the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}}. {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)}}{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} ({{jalink|540|Q30900}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}.{{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} is said to be the place where {{jalink|descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{jalink|three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{jalink|mountain cult|Q93697439}}, where {{jalink|mountain worship|Q93697439}} worshiped {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} itself. The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Hōjomine (Ohachi)}} in July of {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} ({{jalink|788|Q30721}}).After that, {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}}3 years ({{jalink|940|Q23830}}) or {{jalink|Tenryaku|Q1346281}}4 during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Murakami|Q374015}} In the year ({{jalink|950|Q23449}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{jalink|Takachiho River|Q10566710}}, old palace ruins) by {{jalink|Sekora|Q11491623}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the large eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Kajomine (Ohachi)}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{jalink|Kirishima Town|Q6415332}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years..{{jalink|Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|Civilization}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{jalink|Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537}} as a dedication. Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}, the current '''{{jalink|Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''. Respected by the successive {{jalink|Shimazu clan|Q1061406}}, {{jalink|Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727}} was born in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|15 In 1978|Q6707}}) {{jalink|Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{jalink|lottery|Q5433694|a wig}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{jalink|1585|Q6736}}) In June, {{jalink|Yontaka Zenyabo}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{jalink|Arinobu Yamada|Q80475 88}} and again in September, {{jalink|Kiyōyoshi Yoshida}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{jalink|Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450}} visited the {{jalink|Kirishima Mountain Range}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}. Until the {{jalink|Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{jalink|Kirishima Rokusho Gongen}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}. Under the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}), it was ranked as {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (1935) {{jalink|November 16|Q3029}}, after {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}} {{jalink|Yukiyuki|Q11626055}}{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.Also, the {{jalink|sacred tree|Q48743901}} {{jalink|cedar|Q147388|cedar}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}. According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]. === Rituals === Approximately 100 rituals are held annually. * Tsukutachisai (first day of every month) * Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month * Saitan Festival January 1st * Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd) * Genshi Festival January 3rd * Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar) * Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June * Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st * Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August * Regular festival September 19th * New Year's Eve Festival December 31st === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4). === Important cultural property === * Climbing corridor * Imperial Envoy Hall (The following is designated as “attached”) * Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings * 1 sacred food hall File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{jalink|Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{jalink|Shinto architecture|Q3080012}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''. === Precincts === Originally, the {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{jalink|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{jalink|1882|Q7812}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}21 ({{jalink|1946|Q18610}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{jalink|Constitution of Japan|Q237082}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. . File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Ninotorii File:Kirishima Shrine (Torii).jpg|Three Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kaguraden === Access === ; bus *{{jalink|Kyushu Railway|Q498366|JR}}{{jalink|Nippo Main Line|Q1052288}} Get off at {{jalink|Kirishima Jingu Station|Q6415333}} and take the {{jalink|Kagoshima Kotsu|Q11676491}} bus bound for Kirishima Iwasaki Hotel, then take the bus for about 15 minutes. *About 1 hour after taking the Kagoshima Kotsu Kirishima Shrine Access Bus from {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}}. ; car *{{jalink|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803}} Get off at {{jalink|Yokogawa Interchange|Q1655302}}, {{jalink| About 40 minutes via Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50 Makizono Satsuma Line |Q11676950|Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50}} and {{jalink|National Route 223|Q6156973}}. === Documentary === * {{jalink|Welcome to the National Treasure}} "Kirishima Shrine" (September 25, 2022, {{jalink|NHK-BS Premium||NHK-BSP}}) {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Shrine |date=2022-09-25 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=2022-09-25 |accessdate=2022-09-25}} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 25 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{jalink|Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645}}, 1979, pp. 120-121 *Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{jalink|Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 282-283 * "Book of Shinto" {{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|Gakken}}, 1992, p. 227 * Taichi Tatsumiya, Yoko Nakamura, and Haruo Nakano, “Shrines that give you energy - Vol. 6 Kirishima Shrine,” “Psiko” June issue, {{jalink|Poplar Publishing|Q3908386}}, 2006 * "Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture" {{jalink|Kadokawa Shoten|Q1054765}}, 1983 * “Furusato no Osha Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Journal” Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association, 1995 * Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki (eds.), New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary, Tokyodo Publishing, 1997 === Related items === {{WikiCommons|Category:Kirishima-jingu}} {{Osm box|n|2483574061}} * {{jalink|Takachiho Kawara|Q10566710}} * {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}} * {{jalink|Ikko sect|Q5366010}}: {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, {{jalink|Satsuma domain|Q676187}} cracked down on Ikko sect more strictly than {{jalink|Christian|Q718714}}, and the Ikko sect pretended to be parishioners of Kirishima Shrine. * {{jalink|Tanzan Shrine|Q488618}}: A shrine called the “Nikko of Kansai” * {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu Shrine|Q696641}} === External link === * [https://kirishimajingu.or.jp/ Kirishima Jingu] (Jingu official) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirishima Shinkuu}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:鹿児島県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:官幣大社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:鹿児島県の国宝]] [[Category:鹿児島県の重要文化財]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (建造物)]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:霧島市の建築物]] [[Category:霧島市の歴史]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:Need translation]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqq]]

{{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}} |Foundation = Legendary {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} Dynasty ({{jalink|6th century|Q8090}})
Legendary {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} 1st year ({{jalink|540 years|Q30900}}) |Main shrine = {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = Kirishima Rokusha Gongen |Regular festival = {{jalink|September 19th|Q2896}} |Shinto ritual =|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}} of {{jalink|Engishikinaisha}}, and {{jalink|old company rank}} is {{jalink|Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}}Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. . === Enshrined God === The following seven deities are currently enshrined [http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* {{jalink|Ninigi|Q1056017|Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi}} ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Konohananosakuyabime|Q1781862|Konohana Kahimeson}} :* {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hikohihodemison}} :* {{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Himeson}} :* {{jalink|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|Uro Kusabuki Fugoson}} :* {{jalink|Tamayoribime (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayorihime no Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188|Kamiwa Iwayohiko}} === History === [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]] During the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}}. {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)}}{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} ({{jalink|540|Q30900}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}.{{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} is said to be the place where {{jalink|descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{jalink|three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{jalink|mountain cult|Q93697439}}, where {{jalink|mountain worship|Q93697439}} worshiped {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} itself. The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Hōjomine (Ohachi)}} in July of {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} ({{jalink|788|Q30721}}).After that, {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}}3 years ({{jalink|940|Q23830}}) or {{jalink|Tenryaku|Q1346281}}4 during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Murakami|Q374015}} In the year ({{jalink|950|Q23449}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{jalink|Takachiho River|Q10566710}}, old palace ruins) by {{jalink|Sekora|Q11491623}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the large eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Kajomine (Ohachi)}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{jalink|Kirishima Town|Q6415332}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years..{{jalink|Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|Civilization}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{jalink|Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537}} as a dedication. Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}, the current '''{{jalink|Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''. Respected by the successive {{jalink|Shimazu clan|Q1061406}}, {{jalink|Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727}} was born in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|15 In 1978|Q6707}}) {{jalink|Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{jalink|lottery|Q5433694|a wig}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{jalink|1585|Q6736}}) In June, {{jalink|Yontaka Zenyabo}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{jalink|Arinobu Yamada|Q80475 88}} and again in September, {{jalink|Kiyōyoshi Yoshida}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{jalink|Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450}} visited the {{jalink|Kirishima Mountain Range}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}. Until the {{jalink|Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{jalink|Kirishima Rokusho Gongen}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}. Under the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}), it was ranked as {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (1935) {{jalink|November 16|Q3029}}, after {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}} {{jalink|Yukiyuki|Q11626055}}{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.Also, the {{jalink|sacred tree|Q48743901}} {{jalink|cedar|Q147388|cedar}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}. According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]. === Rituals === Approximately 100 rituals are held annually. * Tsukutachisai (first day of every month) * Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month * Saitan Festival January 1st * Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd) * Genshi Festival January 3rd * Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar) * Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June * Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st * Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August * Regular festival September 19th * New Year's Eve Festival December 31st === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4). === Important cultural property === * Climbing corridor * Imperial Envoy Hall (The following is designated as “attached”) * Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings * 1 sacred food hall File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{jalink|Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{jalink|Shinto architecture|Q3080012}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''. === Precincts === Originally, the {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{jalink|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{jalink|1882|Q7812}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}21 ({{jalink|1946|Q18610}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{jalink|Constitution of Japan|Q237082}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. . File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Ninotorii File:Kirishima Shrine (Torii).jpg|Three Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kaguraden === Access === ; bus *{{jalink|Kyushu Railway|Q498366|JR}}{{jalink|Nippo Main Line|Q1052288}} Get off at {{jalink|Kirishima Jingu Station|Q6415333}} and take the {{jalink|Kagoshima Kotsu|Q11676491}} bus bound for Kirishima Iwasaki Hotel, then take the bus for about 15 minutes. *About 1 hour after taking the Kagoshima Kotsu Kirishima Shrine Access Bus from {{jalink|Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310}}. ; car *{{jalink|Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803}} Get off at {{jalink|Yokogawa Interchange|Q1655302}}, {{jalink| About 40 minutes via Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50 Makizono Satsuma Line |Q11676950|Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50}} and {{jalink|National Route 223|Q6156973}}. === Documentary === * {{jalink|Welcome to the National Treasure}} "Kirishima Shrine" (September 25, 2022, {{jalink|NHK-BS Premium||NHK-BSP}}) {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Shrine |date=2022-09-25 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=2022-09-25 |accessdate=2022-09-25}} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 25 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{jalink|Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645}}, 1979, pp. 120-121 *Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{jalink|Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 282-283 * "Book of Shinto" {{jalink|Gakken|Q86741099|Gakken}}, 1992, p. 227 * Taichi Tatsumiya, Yoko Nakamura, and Haruo Nakano, “Shrines that give you energy - Vol. 6 Kirishima Shrine,” “Psiko” June issue, {{jalink|Poplar Publishing|Q3908386}}, 2006 * "Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture" {{jalink|Kadokawa Shoten|Q1054765}}, 1983 * “Furusato no Osha Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Journal” Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association, 1995 * Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki (eds.), New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary, Tokyodo Publishing, 1997 === Related items === {{WikiCommons|Category:Kirishima-jingu}} {{Osm box|n|2483574061}} * {{jalink|Takachiho Kawara|Q10566710}} * {{jalink|Descent of Tenson|Q1084733}} * {{jalink|Ikko sect|Q5366010}}: {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, {{jalink|Satsuma domain|Q676187}} cracked down on Ikko sect more strictly than {{jalink|Christian|Q718714}}, and the Ikko sect pretended to be parishioners of Kirishima Shrine. * {{jalink|Tanzan Shrine|Q488618}}: A shrine called the “Nikko of Kansai” * {{jalink|Nikko Toshogu Shrine|Q696641}} === External link === * [https://kirishimajingu.or.jp/ Kirishima Jingu] (Jingu official) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirishima Shinkuu}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:鹿児島県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:官幣大社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:鹿児島県の国宝]] [[Category:鹿児島県の重要文化財]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (建造物)]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:霧島市の建築物]] [[Category:霧島市の歴史]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:Need translation]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqq]]

Legendary {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} 1st year ({{jalink|540 years|Q30900}}) |Main shrine = {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = Kirishima Rokusha Gongen |Regular festival = {{jalink|September 19th|Q2896}} |Shinto ritual =|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701}}{{jalink|Kirishima City|Q858352}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}} of {{jalink|Engishikinaisha}}, and {{jalink|old company rank}} is {{jalink|Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{jalink|National Treasure|Q1139795}}Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. . === Enshrined God === The following seven deities are currently enshrined [http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* {{jalink|Ninigi|Q1056017|Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi}} ; Aidenjin :* {{jalink|Konohananosakuyabime|Q1781862|Konohana Kahimeson}} :* {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hikohihodemison}} :* {{jalink|Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|Toyota Himeson}} :* {{jalink|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|Uro Kusabuki Fugoson}} :* {{jalink|Tamayoribime (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayorihime no Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188|Kamiwa Iwayohiko}} === History === [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]] During the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}}. {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)}}{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{jalink|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792}} ({{jalink|540|Q30900}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}.{{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} is said to be the place where {{jalink|descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{jalink|three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{jalink|mountain cult|Q93697439}}, where {{jalink|mountain worship|Q93697439}} worshiped {{jalink|Takachihomine|Q3514128}} itself. The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Hōjomine (Ohachi)}} in July of {{jalink|Enryaku|Q1373176}} ({{jalink|788|Q30721}}).After that, {{jalink|Tenkei|Q1327340}}3 years ({{jalink|940|Q23830}}) or {{jalink|Tenryaku|Q1346281}}4 during the reign of {{jalink|Emperor Murakami|Q374015}} In the year ({{jalink|950|Q23449}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{jalink|Takachiho River|Q10566710}}, old palace ruins) by {{jalink|Sekora|Q11491623}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the large eruption of {{jalink|Ohachi|Q11489346|Kajomine (Ohachi)}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{jalink|Kirishima Town|Q6415332}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years..{{jalink|Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|Civilization}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{jalink|Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537}} as a dedication. Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{jalink|Bunryaku|Q1194125}} ({{jalink|1234|Q5424}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{jalink|1484|Q6639}}), {{jalink|Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}}, the current '''{{jalink|Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''. Respected by the successive {{jalink|Shimazu clan|Q1061406}}, {{jalink|Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727}} was born in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|15 In 1978|Q6707}}) {{jalink|Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{jalink|lottery|Q5433694|a wig}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{jalink|1585|Q6736}}) In June, {{jalink|Yontaka Zenyabo}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{jalink|Arinobu Yamada|Q80475 88}} and again in September, {{jalink|Kiyōyoshi Yoshida}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{jalink|Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450}} visited the {{jalink|Kirishima Mountain Range}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}. Until the {{jalink|Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{jalink|Kirishima Rokusho Gongen}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}. Under the {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}), it was ranked as {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}. {{jalink|1935|Q18658}} (1935) {{jalink|November 16|Q3029}}, after {{jalink|Special Army Exercise}}, {{jalink|Emperor Showa|Q34479}} {{jalink|Yukiyuki|Q11626055}}{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.Also, the {{jalink|sacred tree|Q48743901}} {{jalink|cedar|Q147388|cedar}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}. According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]. === Rituals === Approximately 100 rituals are held annually. * Tsukutachisai (first day of every month) * Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month * Saitan Festival January 1st * Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd) * Genshi Festival January 3rd * Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar) * Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June * Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st * Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August * Regular festival September 19th * New Year's Eve Festival December 31st === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4). === Important cultural property === * Climbing corridor * Imperial Envoy Hall (The following is designated as “attached”) * Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings * 1 sacred food hall File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{jalink|Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{jalink|Shinto architecture|Q3080012}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''. === Precincts === Originally, the {{jalink|Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{jalink|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{jalink|1882|Q7812}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}21 ({{jalink|1946|Q18610}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{jalink|Constitution of Japan|Q237082}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. . Legendary {{ill|lt=Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|WD=Q329792}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=540 years|Q30900|WD=Q30900}}) |Main shrine = {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025}} |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = Kirishima Rokusha Gongen |Regular festival = {{ill|lt=September 19th|Q2896|WD=Q2896}} |Shinto ritual =|Map = {{Location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Kirishima Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=200|frame-height=280}} }} '''Kirishima Shrine'' (Kirishima Shrine) is located in {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture|Q15701|WD=Q15701}}{{ill|lt=Kirishima City|Q858352|WD=Q858352}}Kirishima Taguchi. It is {{ill|lt=Ronsha|Q135022904|WD=Q135022904}} of {{ill||lt=Engishikinaisha|UNKNOWN}}, and {{ill||lt=old company rank|UNKNOWN}} is {{ill|lt=Modern company rank system #government shrine|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}[http://www.kagojinjacho.or.jp/search/airaisa/kirishima/post-296.html Kirishima Shrine] - Kagoshima Prefectural Shrine Agency February 27, 2012. The main shrine, shrine hall, and worship hall are designated as {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795}}Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 9 dated February 9, 2020. . === Enshrined God === The following seven deities are currently enshrined [http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html History] (official website). . ; Main enshrined deity :* {{ill|lt=Ninigi|Q1056017|WD=Q1056017|lt=Tenraoseki Kokuroseki Amatsu Hidakahiko Fire Qiong Qionggi}} ; Aidenjin :* {{ill|lt=Konohananosakuyabime|Q1781862|WD=Q1781862|lt=Konohana Kahimeson}} :* {{ill|lt=Hoori|Q1051960|WD=Q1051960|lt=Hikohihodemison}} :* {{ill|lt=Toyota Mahime|Q2329261|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyota Himeson}} :* {{ill|lt=Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|WD=Q1373935|lt=Uro Kusabuki Fugoson}} :* {{ill|lt=Tamayoribime (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|WD=Q3082751|lt=Tamayorihime no Mikoto}} :* {{ill|lt=Emperor Jinmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|lt=Kamiwa Iwayohiko}} === History === [[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Old Palace]] [[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred Cedar]] During the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|WD=Q329792}} (6th century), a monk named Keitane Shonin visited {{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|WD=Q3514128}}. {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|WD=Q11489346|lt=It is said that the shrine building was built on Setao (Setao Hill) between Hijomine (Ohachi)}}{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture |date=1983-03-08 |year=1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}. One theory is that it was founded in the first year of {{ill|lt=Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|WD=Q329792}} ({{ill|lt=540|Q30900|WD=Q30900}}). |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}.{{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|WD=Q3514128}} is said to be the place where {{ill|lt=descendance of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733}} in Japanese mythology, so the gods associated with {{ill|lt=three generations of Hyuga|Q56347075|WD=Q56347075}} are currently enshrined there. However, it is thought that this shrine originally began as a {{ill|lt=mountain cult|Q93697439|WD=Q93697439}}, where {{ill|lt=mountain worship|Q93697439|WD=Q93697439}} worshiped {{ill|lt=Takachihomine|Q3514128|WD=Q3514128}} itself. The original shrine, Setao, was located close to the crater, so the shrine often caught fire due to eruptions, and was destroyed in the eruption of {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|WD=Q11489346|lt=Hōjomine (Ohachi)}} in July of {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176}} ({{ill|lt=788|Q30721|WD=Q30721}}).After that, {{ill|lt=Tenkei|Q1327340|WD=Q1327340}}3 years ({{ill|lt=940|Q23830|WD=Q23830}}) or {{ill|lt=Tenryaku|Q1346281|WD=Q1346281}}4 during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Murakami|Q374015|WD=Q374015}} In the year ({{ill|lt=950|Q23449|WD=Q23449}}), it was rebuilt in Setaogoe (currently {{ill|lt=Takachiho River|Q10566710|WD=Q10566710}}, old palace ruins) by {{ill|lt=Sekora|Q11491623|WD=Q11491623}} Shonin, but this place has also been rebuilt many times. In the first year of {{ill|lt=Bunryaku|Q1194125|WD=Q1194125}} ({{ill|lt=1234|Q5424|WD=Q5424}}), the large eruption of {{ill|lt=Ohachi|Q11489346|WD=Q11489346|lt=Kajomine (Ohachi)}} caused the shrine buildings, monk's quarters, etc. was completely destroyed by fire, so a "temporary shrine" was built at Tachiyo in Kirishima Taguchi (next to Kirishima Junior High School, bordering the {{ill|lt=Kirishima Town|Q6415332|WD=Q6415332}} ground), where it was worshiped for about 250 years..{{ill|lt=Civilization_(Japan)|Q1193544|WD=Q1193544|lt=Civilization}} In 16 years ({{ill|lt=1484|Q6639|WD=Q6639}}), Kenkei Shonin rebuilt the current Kirishima Shrine on the orders of {{ill|lt=Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874|WD=Q11162874}}. However, the shrine building went up in flames many times after that, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1715|Q6884}} by {{ill|lt=Yoshitaka Shimazu|Q11246537|WD=Q11246537}} as a dedication. Another theory is that after the shrine building was destroyed by an eruption in the first year of {{ill|lt=Bunryaku|Q1194125|WD=Q1194125}} ({{ill|lt=1234|Q5424|WD=Q5424}}), the shrine building was moved to Mt. Nagao (the current location of Higashi Kirishima Shrine) east of {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|WD=Q1319361}}. (Japan)|Q1193544|Bunmei}} In 16 years ({{ill|lt=1484|Q6639|WD=Q6639}}), {{ill|lt=Shimazu Tadamasa|Q11162874|WD=Q11162874}} called it "Tosha" ('''Kirishima It is said that it was divided into two shrines: Higashi Gozaisho Gongen''' (currently 'Kirishima Higashi Shrine') and 'West Shrine' ('''Nishi Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen''', currently 'Kirishima Jingu''').{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary |date=1997-09-25 |year=1997 |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing}}.In addition to this, after moving the shrine building to Mt. Nagao to the east of {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|WD=Q1319361}}, the current '''{{ill|lt=Kirishima Shrine|Q11660876|WD=Q11660876}}'' and '''Mist There is also a theory that it was divided into two shrines, ``Shimahigashi Shrine'' and ``Kirishimanishi Shrine'' (currently ``Kirishima Jingu'') from ``Kirishimahigashi Shrine''. Respected by the successive {{ill|lt=Shimazu clan|Q1061406|WD=Q1061406}}, {{ill|lt=Yoshihisa Shimazu|Q955727|WD=Q955727}} was born in {{ill|lt=Tensho|Q1145058|WD=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|lt=15 In 1978|Q6707|WD=Q6707}}) {{ill|lt=Battle of Mimikawa|Q4871739|WD=Q4871739}}, he visited a shrine and drew a {{ill|lt=lottery|Q5433694|WD=Q5433694|lt=a wig}}, and also in 14th year of Tensho (1978) when he moved north to Kyushu. {{ill|lt=1585|Q6736|WD=Q6736}}) In June, {{ill||lt=Yontaka Zenyabo|UNKNOWN}} of Sosaki Tatsucho and his senior retainer {{ill||lt=Arinobu Yamada|UNKNOWN}} and again in September, {{ill||lt=Kiyōyoshi Yoshida|UNKNOWN}}, respectively, to draw the wig and decide on the direction of the invasion.He often seeks divine counsel when making important decisions.{{Source required|date=February 2022}}.It is also known that {{ill|lt=Ryoma Sakamoto|Q378450|WD=Q378450}} visited the {{ill||lt=Kirishima Mountain Range|UNKNOWN}} on what is said to be Japan's first honeymoon, but by that time he was already at the top of the mountain. Ryoma Sakamoto{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|New character old kana|Letter - December 4, Keio 2, addressed to Otome Sakamoto-}}. Until the {{ill||lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Ordinance|UNKNOWN}} was issued during the Meiji period, it was called ``West Gozaisho Kirishima Gongen,'' and the main hall was an eleven-faced Kannon. It has Karinji Temple in Bettoji Temple. It played a central role in {{ill||lt=Kirishima Rokusho Gongen|UNKNOWN}} worship by Shugen monks centered on Mt. Kirishima.{{Citation required|date=February 2022}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534}}, in February 1874|Q7761}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}}), it was ranked as {{ill|lt=Modern Shrine Ranking System#Kansha|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}. {{ill|lt=1935|Q18658|WD=Q18658}} (1935) {{ill|lt=November 16|Q3029|WD=Q3029}}, after {{ill||lt=Special Army Exercise|UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Emperor Showa|Q34479|WD=Q34479}} {{ill|lt=Yukiyuki|Q11626055|WD=Q11626055}}{{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Takeshi Hara |title=Complete record of Emperor Showa's train |publisher=Shinchosha |date=2016-09-30 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}.Also, the {{ill|lt=sacred tree|Q48743901|WD=Q48743901}} {{ill|lt=cedar|Q147388|WD=Q147388|lt=cedar}} is estimated to be about 800 years old, and is said to be the ancestor of the cedars of southern Kyushu {{citation needed|date=February 2022}}. According to a government report on February 9, 2020, the "Honden, Heiden, and Worship Hall" were designated as national treasures [https://www.city-kirishima.jp/bunka/kyoiku/rekishi/bunkazai/shittebunkazai/bunka-kirishima.html Kirishima City Official Homepage Overview of Designated Cultural Properties [Kirishima]]. === Rituals === Approximately 100 rituals are held annually. * Tsukutachisai (first day of every month) * Monthly Festival (Tsukinamisai) 19th of every month * Saitan Festival January 1st * Hatsunikkusai (January 2nd) * Genshi Festival January 3rd * Uchimaki Festival February 18th (January 1st in the lunar calendar) * Rice planting festival March 3rd (February 4th in the lunar calendar) * Sanada's Nagata Rice Planting Festival (Sanada's Osada Otauesai) First Sunday of June * Great Purification Ceremony June 30th, December 31st * Minamikyushu Kagura Last Saturday of August * Regular festival September 19th * New Year's Eve Festival December 31st === Cultural assets === === National Treasure === * 1 main hall, 1 hall of worship, and 2 attached building tags (buildings) - Designated on February 9, 2022 (Reiwa 4). === Important cultural property === * Climbing corridor * Imperial Envoy Hall (The following is designated as “attached”) * Kadomori Shrine 2 buildings * 1 sacred food hall File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Imperial Envoy Hall (side) File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Shrine of Worship File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Noboriro The shrine building mentioned above was donated by the Kagoshima feudal lord {{ill|lt=Yoshiki Shimazu|Q11246537|WD=Q11246537}} and was built in 1715. The shrine buildings are all ornately painted in vermilion. The interior of the main hall in particular is luxuriously decorated, with pillars, beams, and long pillars all painted with vermilion lacquer, important points decorated with colored patterns and plated decorative metal fittings, and walls decorated with panels with richly colored reliefs. {{ill|lt=Shinto architecture|Q3080012|WD=Q3080012}} It is rare to find such elaborate decorations not only on the outside but also on the inside, and it has another name: ``Nikko of the West''. === Precincts === Originally, the {{ill|lt=Mt. Kirishima|Q1319361|WD=Q1319361}} area was the precincts of Kirishima Shrine, but in 1871|Q7746}}, {{j alink|Abolition of feudal domains|Q331905}} Prefectural borders were drawn along the top of Mt. Kirishima, and the {{ill|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300|WD=Q130300}} side was excluded from the shrine precincts. In Meiji 15 ({{ill|lt=1882|Q7812|WD=Q7812}}), the area was further reduced by 7,810 hectares, and in {{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567}}21 ({{ill|lt=1946|Q18610|WD=Q18610}}), most of the forest became state-owned land with the enactment of the {{ill|lt=Constitution of Japan|Q237082|WD=Q237082}}, which turned it into a religious corporation. Later, 789 hectares needed for festival events were returned to the shrine.Kirishima Town Local History, edited by Kirishima Town Local History Editorial Committee, Kirishima Town, 1992. . File:KirishimaJingu_04.jpg|Ninotorii File:Kirishima Shrine (Torii).jpg|Three Torii File:KirishimaJingu_02.jpg|New Kagura Hall File:KirishimaJingu6816.jpg|New Kaguraden === Access === ; bus *{{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR}}{{ill|lt=Nippo Main Line|Q1052288|WD=Q1052288}} Get off at {{ill|lt=Kirishima Jingu Station|Q6415333|WD=Q6415333}} and take the {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Kotsu|Q11676491|WD=Q11676491}} bus bound for Kirishima Iwasaki Hotel, then take the bus for about 15 minutes. *About 1 hour after taking the Kagoshima Kotsu Kirishima Shrine Access Bus from {{ill|lt=Kagoshima Airport|Q1156310|WD=Q1156310}}. ; car *{{ill|lt=Kyushu Expressway|Q1060803|WD=Q1060803}} Get off at {{ill|lt=Yokogawa Interchange|Q1655302|WD=Q1655302}}, {{ill|lt=About 40 minutes via Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50 Makizono Satsuma Line|Q11676950|WD=Q11676950|lt=Kagoshima Prefectural Route 50}} and {{ill|lt=National Route 223|Q6156973|WD=Q6156973}}. === Documentary === * {{ill||lt=Welcome to the National Treasure|UNKNOWN}} "Kirishima Shrine" (September 25, 2022, {{ill|lt=NHK-BS Premium||WD=|lt=NHK-BSP}}) {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/LJ77715Y29/episode/te/V9GY3767MJ/ |title=(12) Kirishima Shrine |date=2022-09-25 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wJAH3 |archivedate=2022-09-25 |accessdate=2022-09-25}} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 25 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645}}, 1979, pp. 120-121 *Shunpei Ueyama et al., “Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines” {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312}}, 1992, pp. 282-283 * "Book of Shinto" {{ill|lt=Gakken|Q86741099|WD=Q86741099|lt=Gakken}}, 1992, p. 227 * Taichi Tatsumiya, Yoko Nakamura, and Haruo Nakano, “Shrines that give you energy - Vol. 6 Kirishima Shrine,” “Psiko” June issue, {{ill|lt=Poplar Publishing|Q3908386|WD=Q3908386}}, 2006 * "Kadokawa Japanese Place Name Dictionary 46 Kagoshima Prefecture" {{ill|lt=Kadokawa Shoten|Q1054765|WD=Q1054765}}, 1983 * “Furusato no Osha Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Journal” Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association, 1995 * Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki (eds.), New Popular Edition Shrine Dictionary, Tokyodo Publishing, 1997 === Related items === {{WikiCommons|Category:Kirishima-jingu}} {{Osm box|n|2483574061}} * {{ill|lt=Takachiho Kawara|Q10566710|WD=Q10566710}} * {{ill|lt=Descent of Tenson|Q1084733|WD=Q1084733}} * {{ill|lt=Ikko sect|Q5366010|WD=Q5366010}}: {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963}}, {{ill|lt=Satsuma domain|Q676187|WD=Q676187}} cracked down on Ikko sect more strictly than {{ill|lt=Christian|Q718714|WD=Q718714}}, and the Ikko sect pretended to be parishioners of Kirishima Shrine. * {{ill|lt=Tanzan Shrine|Q488618|WD=Q488618}}: A shrine called the “Nikko of Kansai” * {{ill|lt=Nikko Toshogu Shrine|Q696641|WD=Q696641}} === External link === * [https://kirishimajingu.or.jp/ Kirishima Jingu] (Jingu official) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirishima Shinkuu}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Kirishima Jingu]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:鹿児島県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:官幣大社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:鹿児島県の国宝]] [[Category:鹿児島県の重要文化財]] [[Category:日本の国宝 (建造物)]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:霧島市の建築物]] [[Category:霧島市の歴史]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqq]]
